prompt_text: I need a new air conditioner installed in Atlanta. Which specific HVAC companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
Good — I’ll give you a short list of specific companies to call in Atlanta plus why each is worth contacting, then a quick checklist of what to ask so you can compare quotes.

Recommended companies to call
- Coolray (large Atlanta-based HVAC/plumbing company)
  - Why: Big local footprint, lots of technicians in the Atlanta area (faster scheduling/response), offers installations, maintenance plans and financing. Good option if you want broad local support and emergency service.

- One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning (Atlanta franchise)
  - Why: National brand with a local franchise model; they advertise on-time service guarantees and standardized installation processes. Useful when you want predictable timelines and a national warranty/standards backing a local crew.

- Service Experts Heating & Air Conditioning (Atlanta location)
  - Why: National chain with trained technicians, financing options, and service/maintenance plans. They often handle manufacturer warranties and larger replacement projects well.

- Manufacturer-authorized dealers for Trane, Carrier, Lennox (search each brand’s “Find a Dealer” for Atlanta)
  - Why: Authorized dealers install to factory specifications, register full manufacturer warranties, and have factory training. If you prefer a specific brand (e.g., Trane or Carrier), call the brand’s local authorized dealer.

- A top-rated independent Atlanta contractor (look for local names with strong reviews)
  - Why: Independent contractors can be more flexible on pricing and personalized service. Many local shops have excellent reputations for quality installs and follow-up service. Search Google/Angie’s List/Yelp/BBB for top-rated independent installers in your zip code.

Why these categories, briefly
- Local large companies (Coolray, One Hour, Service Experts) combine quick availability, standard processes and financing.
- Manufacturer-authorized dealers give the best warranty/brand support if you want a Trane/Carrier/Lennox.
- Independent reputable contractors can offer competitive pricing and personalized attention.

What to ask every company (use this to compare quotes)
1. Do you have a Georgia HVAC license and NATE-certified installers? Can you provide license numbers and proof of insurance?  
2. Do you do a Manual J load calculation for proper sizing (not a rule-of-thumb)? Will that be included in the written quote?  
3. Which brands/models do you recommend and why? What SEER will you propose?  
4. Is the installer factory-authorized for the brand you’re proposing? Will you register the full manufacturer warranty?  
5. What is included in the written estimate (unit, labor, drain/duct work, permits, disposal, thermostat, start-up, refrigerant, line set, permit fees)?  
6. Do you provide a written workmanship warranty in addition to the manufacturer warranty? How long?  
7. Do you offer financing, rebates, or maintenance plans? Any available utility or manufacturer rebates?  
8. Will you pull permits and handle inspections?  
9. Timeline: when can you start and how long will the install take?  
10. Ask for three local references or recent installs similar to yours and check online reviews.

Red flags
- Pushy sales only emphasizing monthly payment without full quote details.  
- No Manual J or no written estimate.  
- Technician can’t produce license/insurance or refuses to register the warranty.  
- Very low bid that seems too good to be true (likely cut corners or hidden fees).

If you want, I can:
- Draft a short phone script/email you can use when calling the companies.  
- Help you evaluate two or three written quotes if you paste them here.  
- Narrow the vendor list to specific dealer names and phone numbers if you give me your Atlanta ZIP code (I’ll provide guidance on how to verify each one).

Which of the options above would you like help with next?
